target.title: fix(cron): persist due-job outcomes incrementally
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a cron job of kind `agentTurn` completes, the `running_at_ms` field in the cron store was not immediately reset. Outcomes from completed due-jobs were buffered in memory until `Promise.all(workers)` resolved, leaving `runningAtMs` set on persisted records. This blocked the job from future scheduling because `isRunnableJob` returns false when `runningAtMs` is a number.

Fixes [#100471](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/100471)

## Why This Change Was Made

The root cause: `onTimer` collected all due-job outcomes into an array and applied them to the cron store only after every worker finished. If a later job in the same due batch was still running or wedged, earlier completed jobs remained with `runningAtMs` set and could not be scheduled again.

This change makes each worker persist its completed outcome immediately under the cron store lock, rather than buffering until the entire batch drains.

## User Impact

- Cron jobs that complete while other due jobs are still running will be immediately freed for future scheduling.
- No more manual SQL reset of `running_at_ms` or gateway restart required.
- No config or API changes.

## Evidence

- All 160 cron service tests pass (15 test files)
- `git diff --check` passes
- `pnpm build` passes with Node 22.19
- Two new regression tests added covering:
  - Completed job removed from persisted store before blocking job finishes
  - Queued due-job running markers preserved during incremental batch persistence
